comparisons.peer_topic: Investment Manager Relationship and Fee Structure
comparisons.peer_summary: The firm forms nonconsolidated investment funds with third-party investors, acting as investment manager to receive management, advisory, and incentive fees, while also investing alongside clients in certain funds.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi (C) and Goldman Sachs (GS) explicitly disclose acting as investment managers for formed investment funds. Citi establishes these funds specifically as opportunities for qualified employees to invest in private equity, providing recourse and non-recourse financing. In contrast, GS forms nonconsolidated investment funds with third-party investors (not limited to employees) and acts as the investment manager to receive management, advisory, and incentive fees. While both act as investment managers for similar structures (private equity/alternative investments), the beneficiary group (employees vs. third parties) and the primary economic driver described (financing provision vs. fee generation) differ.

sentences.text: Citi has also established a number of investment funds as opportunities for qualified employees to invest in private equity investments.
The Company acts as investment manager for these funds and may provide employees with financing on both recourse and non-recourse bases for a portion of the employees' investment commitments.
The firm has formed nonconsolidated investment funds with third-party investors.
As the firm generally acts as the investment manager for these funds, it is entitled to receive management fees and, in certain cases, advisory fees or incentive fees from these funds.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm sponsors non-consolidated investment management funds for third-party investors, acting as general partner and investment adviser, and holds contractual capital commitments, guarantees, and counterparty arrangements related to these funds.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Morgan Stanley (MS) disclose involvement in managing non-consolidated investment funds. Citi manages funds for qualified employees in private equity and provides financing. MS sponsors non-consolidated investment management funds for third-party investors, acting as general partner and investment adviser, and typically commits its own capital as a minority investor. Both entities serve in the investment manager/adviser role for these funds, but Citi's disclosure highlights employee participation and financing terms, whereas MS highlights third-party sponsorship, minority capital commitment, and contractual arrangements.

sentences.text: Citi has also established a number of investment funds as opportunities for qualified employees to invest in private equity investments.
The Company acts as investment manager for these funds and may provide employees with financing on both recourse and non-recourse bases for a portion of the employees' investment commitments.

The Firm sponsors several non-consolidated investment management funds for third-party investors where it typically acts as general partner of, and investment adviser to, these funds and typically commits to invest a minority of the capital of such funds, with subscribing third-party investors contributing the majority.
The Firm has contractual capital commitments, guarantees and counterparty arrangements with respect to these investment management funds.
